la:verb:languesco.gloss: to become faint, feeble, weak, languid or sick; to languish
senses: to become faint, feeble, weak, languid or sick; to languish
la:verb:languesco.html:
languesco, gŭi, 3,
v. inch. n. [langueo], to become faint, weak, languid (class.; syn.: torpesco, marcesco).
Lit.
In gen.: corpore languescit,: orator metuo ne languescat senectute,: corpora,; : vites languescunt,: cum flos, succisus aratro, languescit moriens,droops, withers,: Bacchus in amphora Languescit, becomes mild or mellow, : luna languescit,becomes obscured,: color in luteum languescens,inclining to,.—
In partic., to be enfeebled by disease, to be ill, to languish (poet. and post-Aug.): nec mea languescent corpora,: ter omnino per quatuordecim annos languit,.—
Trop., to grow languid, listless, or inactive, to decline, decrease: consensus populi, si nos languescimus debilitetur necesse est,: Martia legio hoc nuntio languescet et mollietur,: quare non est, cur eorum spes infringatur aut languescat industria,should relax,: militaria studia,are on the decline,: affectus omnes,: mens languescit,: omnium rerum cupido languescit, cum facilis occasio est, : paulatim atrocibus irae languescunt animis,: illa rabies languit,.

la:noun:languor.html:
languor, ōris, m.
langueo
,
faintness, feebleness, weariness, sluggishness, languor, lassitude.
Lit.
In gen. (class.; cf.: torpor, torpedo, veturnus): ubi saepe ad languorem tua duritia dederis octo validos lictores. : haec deambulatio me ad languorem dedit,has fatigued me,: (animus) cum languore corporis nec membris uti nec sensibus potest,on account of lassitude of the body,: languore militum et vigiliis periculum augetur,.— In plur., .—Transf., of things, of the faintness, paleness of colors, .—Poet., of the sea, stillness, calmness: et maria pigro fixa languore impulit,.—
In partic., faintness, weakness, languor proceeding from disease (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): aquosus,dropsy,: languor faucium,: in languorem incidit,: ipsum languorem peperit cibus imperfectus,: vere languores nostros ipse tulit,: a languoribus sanari,.—
Trop., faintness, dulness, sluggishness, apathy, inactivity, listlessness (class.): languori se desidiaeque dedere,: languorem afferre alicui, opp. acuere,; : bonorum,: in languorem vertere,: amantem languor Arguit,; cf. .

la:verb:lanio.html:
lănĭo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
etym. dub.; cf. lacer, δάκνω
,
to tear or rend in pieces, to mangle, lacerate (class.; cf.: lacero, discerpo, dilanio).
Lit.: hominem,: corpora a feris laniata,: lanianda viscera praebere,: laniando dentibus hostem exspirare,: foede crura brachiaque,: vestem,: vestes,: Priamiden laniatum corpore toto vidit,: digitis ora,: carmen,—With Gr. acc.: flavos Lavinia crinīs, Et roseas laniata genas,: comas,.—Transf., poet.: venti mundum laniant,: laniata classis,.—
Trop. (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): et tua sacrilegae laniarunt carmina linguae,: vitia cor laniant,.

la:verb:laniatus.gloss: a tearing in pieces, a mangling, lacerating
senses: a tearing in pieces, a mangling, lacerating
la:verb:laniatus.html:
lănĭātus, ūs, m.
1. lanio
,
a tearing in pieces, a mangling, lacerating.
Lit. (rare but class.): ferarum, *: avium,.—In plur.: avium ferarumque laniatibus objectus,: quid efferatius quam quod membra et artus debitoris brevissimo laniatu distrahantur,.—
Trop., anguish, remorse: si recludantur tyrannorum mentes, posse adspici laniatus,.

la:noun:lanx.html:
lanx, lancis, f.
cf. λέκος, λεκάνη
,
a plate, platter, charger, dish (class.; cf.: patina, patella, magis, scutula).
In gen.: in lancibus,: in filicatis lancibus,: pomum de caelata sumere lance,: cumulantque oneratis lancibus aras,: inter lances mensasque nitentes,: rotundae lances,: qui furtum quaerere velit, nudus quaerat, linteo cinctus, lancem habens, etc., sqq.; cf. Paul. ex Müll.; ; : sic implet leves scutulas, cavasque lances,; : squilla distendat pectore lancem,.—
In partic., the scale of a balance (cf.: libra, statera, trutina): necesse est lancem in libra ponderibus impositis deprimi,: Critolaus cum in alteram lancem animi bona imponat, in alteram corporis et externa, etc.,; cf. ; cf.: Juppiter ipse duas aequato examine lances Sustinet,: cum in altera lance Claudius et Nero starent, in altera, etc.,.—
Trop.: vitam aequa lance pensitare, to weigh or consider impartially, : aequa lance examinare,: paripendere lance cunctos,: aequa lance servari,i. e. in like manner,.

la:noun:lanugo.gloss: woolly substance, the down of plants, of youthful cheeks, etc.
senses: woolly substance, the down of plants, of youthful cheeks, etc.
la:noun:lanugo.html:
lānūgo, ĭnis, f.
cf. Gr. λάχνη, Lat. lāna
,
woolly substance, down, of plants, of the cheeks, etc. (poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
Lit.: flaventem primā ianugine malas Dum sequeris Clytium,; so, primaque par sacrae lanugo senectae,; cf.: comae graciles et lanuginis instar,: signarat dubia teneras lanugine malas,: a prima lanugine,: herba cubile praebebat, multa et molli lanugine abundans,: folia araneosa lanugine obducta,: cana legam tenera lanugine mala,.—
Transf., sawdust, .

la:noun:lancea.gloss: The Roman auxiliaries' short javelin; a light spear or lance.
senses: The Roman auxiliaries' short javelin; a light spear or lance.
la:noun:lancea.html:
lancĕa, ae, f.
λόγχη, acc. to Paul. ex Müll.; acc. to Varr. ap. , of Spanish origin
,
a light spear, with a leather thong fastened to the middle of it, a lance, spear (cf.: telum, spiculum, hastile, pilum, jaculum, etc.): Suevi lanceis configunt, Sisenn. ap. : lancea infesta ... medium femur trajecit voluseni,: ceteri sparos aut lanceas portabant,: Romanus miles missili pilo aut lanceis assultans,; : lata,i. e. with a broad head,; : cujus torta manu commisit lancea bellum,; : haec, duas lanceas dextra praeferens,: mihi non parvam incussisti sollicitudinem, injecto non scrupulo, sed lancea, ne sermones nostros anus illa cognoscat,i. e. great dread,.

lancea

la:adj:languidus.html:
languĭdus, a, um, adj.
langueo
,
faint, weak, dull, sluggish, languid (class.; cf.: lassus, fessus, fatigatus, defessus).
Lit.
In gen.: homines vino languidi,; cf.: vino vigiliisque languidus,: pecus,: boves Collo trahentes languido,.—Transf., of things: (oculi) languidi et torpentes,dull,; cf.: vultus non languidus,: flumen,sluggish,; so, aqua,: ventus,gentle, mild;; cf. carbasa,hanging loose, not swelled out,: color,pale,: ignis,: ictus venarum,: arbor piri,; .—Comp.: languidioribus nostris vallum scindere (hostes),: folia languidiora,: vina,i. e. more mellow,.—
In partic., faint, weak, languid from sickness, languishing, ill (poet. and in postAug. prose): lumina, Laurea Tullius poët. ap. : languidior noster si quando est Paulus,: uxor,.—Subst.: languĭdus, i, m., the sick man, invalid, ; —
Trop., faint, feeble, powerless, inactive, listless, of persons and things: senectus languida atque iners,: philosophus mollis, languidus, enervatus,: si qui antea aut alieniores fuerant aut languidiores,more sluggish,; cf.: nos etiam languidiores postea facti sumus,: illi beati, quos nullae futtiles laetitiae exultantes languidis liquefaciunt voluptatibus,; : esse remisso ac languido animo,: languidiore credo studio in causa fuistis,: oratio languidior,: auctoritas patrum,weak,: Romani ... fessi lassique erant: tamen instructi intentique obviam procedebant. Nam dolus Numidarum nihil languidi neque remissi patiebatur,: oculos ubi languida pressit quies,producing languor,.—Sup. seems not to occur. —Hence, adv.: languĭdē, in a languid manner, faintly, feebly, slowly, languidly (class.): procedere,: nutare,: agere,: palmae languide dulces,slightly,. —Comp.: languidius in opere versari,: dictum languidius,more faintheartedly, spiritlessly,.— Sup. seems not to occur.

la:verb:langueo.html:
languĕo, ēre, 2, v. n.
root lag-; Gr. λαγαρός, λάγνος, lewd; Lat. laxare, lactes; cf. Sanscr. lang-a, prostitute; Gr. λαγώς, hare, λαγόνες, the flanks, womb
,
to be faint, weary, languid (cf.: languesco, marceo, torpeo).
Lit.
In gen.: cum de via languerem,was fatigued with my journey,: per assiduos motus languere,to be wearied,.—Poet.: flos languet,droops, : languet aequor,the sea is calm,: lunae languet jubar,is enfeebled, obscured,.—
In partic., to be weak, faint, languid from disease (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): languent mea membra,: tristi languebunt corpora morbo,: sub natalem suum plerumque languebat,: si te languere audierimus, Aug. ap. : ego langui et aegrotavi per dies,; ; cf. languesco.—
Trop., to be languid, dull, heavy, inactive, listless: languet juventus, nec perinde atque debebat in laudis et gloriae cupiditate versatur,: nec eam solitudinem languere patior,to pass in idleness, to be wasted,: otio,; cf.: in otio hebescere et languere,: si paululum modo vos languere viderint,to be without energy,: languet amor,: mihi gratia languet,.—Hence, languens, entis, P. a., faint, weak, feeble, inert, powerless, inactive, languid: incitare languentes,; cf.: commovere languentem : nostris languentibus atque animo remissis,: languenti stomacho esse, Cael. ap. : irritamentum Veneris languentis,: vox languens,: cor,: hyacinthus,drooping,; so, ramus,.

la:noun:lana.html:
lāna, ae, f.
Gr. λάχνη, λάχνος, λῆνος, Dor. λᾶνος; cf. λάοιος, and v. Müll.
,
wool, ; ; ; : lanam cārĕre,to card wool,; so, lanam trahere,: lanam deducere,: lanas ducere,to spin wool,: lanam expediendam conducere,for carding and spinning,: lanas tingere murice,to dye,; cf.: lanam fucare veneno Assyrio,: medicata fuco,: aurea lana,the golden fleece,: lana legata, sive succida sive lota sit, sive pectinata sive versicoloria, legato cedit,; cf. § 85: si ex lana mea vestimentum feceris, etc.,.—
Transf.
In gen., a working in wool: lana et tela victum quaeritans,: Lucretia lanae dedita,: lanam facere,.—Plur.: te lanae ... non citharae decent,: admotaque lanis quae cessat acu,.—Prov.: cogitare de lana sua, to be thinking about her work, i. e. to be unconcerned, .—
Of things resembling wool, soft hair or feathers, down: lana leporina et anserina et caprina,; : celantur simili ventura Cydonia lana,; cf. .—Of thin, fleecy clouds: tenuia lanae vellera,; cf. .—Prov.: rixari de lana caprina,i. e. to dispute about trifles,.

la:verb:lancino.gloss: to rend, mangle, lacerate (tear to pieces)
senses: to rend, mangle, lacerate (tear to pieces)
la:verb:lancino.html:
lancĭno, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
cf. lacer

Lit.: alium ira in cubili suo confodit ... alium intra leges celebrisque spectaculum fori lancinavit, Sen. de Ira, 1, 2, 2: morsu aliquem,: conjux membratim lancinatur,: tot sinus Pelopennesi oram lancinant,indent, cut up,.—
Trop., to destroy, consume, waste: : vitam (al. lanciniare),to fritter away, waste,: credulitatem facetiis jocularibus,.

la:noun:lanista.gloss: a trainer or manager of a team of gladiators
senses: a trainer or manager of a team of gladiators
an inciter, instigator (someone who stimulates to violence)
la:noun:lanista.html:
lănista, ae, m.,
a trainer of gladiators, fencing-master (class.; cf.: gladiator, athleta, pugil).
Lit.: num ille lanista omnino jam a gladiatore recessisse videtur,: reus, tamquam clemens lanista,: regia verba lanistae,: circumforaneus,: lanistarum familias ex urbe expellere,; .—So of fowls: rixosarum avium,.—
Transf., an inciter, instigator, agitator; one who stimulates to wrong or violence: hic se ad eum lanistam contulit,: ne videret unius corporis duas acies, lanista Cicerone, dimicantes. Ego lanista?: lanistis Aetolis dimicare,.
